Volt-Temi — API Documentation

Volt-Temi

Volt-Temi is an Android application for the temi robot that provides an interactive map-based way-finding experience. A user picks a destination from a visual map or by speaking its name, and temi navigates there autonomously.

High-level architecture

The app is organized around a set of cooperating managers, each owning one slice of behavior and one slice of UI. Each manager exposes a small interface to MainActivity, which is responsible only for wiring them together.

PackageResponsibility
com.example.volt.mapRenders the floor map, destination markers, pin-buttons, zoom and highlight.
com.example.volt.popupSliding popup with destination details ("Go now" / "Add to list").
com.example.volt.selectedThe user's reorderable list of selected destinations (drag/drop/swipe).
com.example.volt.searchText search over destinations.
com.example.volt.voiceTwo-step voice flow: capture utterance, ask for yes/no confirmation, dispatch.
com.example.volt.currentpositionTracks and renders the robot's current position on the map.
com.example.volt.specialdestinationsAlgorithms for picking auto-suggested destinations (e.g. aerial-distance).
com.example.volt.statusStatus-bar messages: battery, lifting, dragging, repose.
com.example.volt.commnadCommand objects that decouple UI events from the actions they trigger.
com.example.volt.modelPlain domain types (e.g. Destination).
com.example.volt.screenScreen-level views (FAQ, screen manager).
com.example.volt.audioAudio playback hooks.
com.example.volt.exitControlled-exit handling.

Reading the docs

Every public class and method carries a small spec block — a pattern borrowed from MIT 6.031:

  • requires: the precondition the caller must satisfy.
  • modifies: the state that may be mutated by this call.
  • effects: what the call observably does.

Class headers additionally state the Representation Invariant (what must always be true about the object's internal state) and the Abstraction Function (how the internal fields map onto the conceptual thing the class represents). Read those two first to understand any class.
